702487.t: From Proto-Hellenic *gʷəlnō, from Proto-Indo-European *gʷl̥-ne-h₁-, nasal-infix from *gʷelH- (“to hit by throwing”). Cognates are uncertain, but compare Sanskrit उद्गूर्ण (ud-gūrṇa) and Old Irish at·baill (“dies”).

702445.t: The present stem is from Proto-Hellenic *gʷəňňō, from Proto-Indo-European *gʷm̥yéti, from zero-grade of *gʷem- + *-yéti. Cognates include Old English cuman (English come), Latin veniō, and Sanskrit गन्ति॑ (gánti).

702459.t: Uncertain. Beekes proposes a possible pre-form *Βακτήρ (*Baktḗr), which may relate to βάκτρον (báktron) in the same manner as ἀροτήρ (arotḗr) connects to ἄροτρον (árotron).

702477.t: From Proto-Hellenic *gʷə́lanos, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *gʷelh₂- (“acorn”); see there for cognates. Probably unrelated to Ancient Greek βαλανεῖον (bălăneîon, “bath, bathroom”).

702486.t: Unknown. According to Beekes the word is perhaps Pre-Greek, in view of the variation -λλ-/-λ-.
